title: Sobhuza I becomes king
description: Sobhuza I, nicknamed Somhlolo, consolidates the Ngwane kingdom and absorbs neighbouring clans through the turmoil of the Mfecane.

title: Mswati II becomes king
description: Mswati II, remembered as the greatest of the Swazi fighting kings, comes to the throne; the country later takes his name.

title: Pretoria Convention
description: Britain and the restored Transvaal guarantee the independence of Swaziland and its boundaries.

title: London Convention
description: A further convention between Britain and the South African Republic again recognises Swaziland as an independent country under King Mbandzeni.

title: Placed under Transvaal
description: A new Anglo-Boer convention hands Swaziland, riddled with land concessions, to the South African Republic as a protectorate.

title: Sobhuza II becomes king
description: The infant Sobhuza II succeeds King Bhunu with his grandmother Labotsibeni as regent; his reign will be among the longest in history.

title: British protectorate
description: After the Boer defeat, Swaziland becomes a British protectorate governed by a resident commissioner under the High Commissioner in South Africa.

title: Land partition
description: The British carry out a partition that leaves barely a third of the land for the Swazi nation, a loss Sobhuza II will contest for decades.

title: Sobhuza II installed
description: After two decades of regency, Sobhuza II is formally installed as Ingwenyama, head of the Swazi nation.

title: Imbokodvo wins elections
description: The king's Imbokodvo National Movement wins every seat in the pre-independence elections and the British recognise Sobhuza as king.

title: Independence
description: Swaziland becomes independent as a constitutional monarchy under King Sobhuza II.

title: Constitution repealed
description: After the opposition wins seats in the 1972 election, Sobhuza II repeals the constitution, dissolves parliament and rules by decree.

title: Tinkhundla constitution
description: A new constitution establishes the tinkhundla system of representation through local councils dominated by the king's men.

title: Sobhuza II dies
description: Sobhuza II dies after more than eighty years on the throne, and a regency under Queen Dzeliwe follows.

title: Mswati III crowned
description: The eighteen-year-old Mswati III is enthroned as king and Ingwenyama, inheriting Africa's last absolute monarchy.

title: General strike
description: The trade union federation leads a major general strike demanding democratic reform.

title: Country renamed eSwatini
description: Marking fifty years since independence, Mswati III announces that Swaziland is renamed the Kingdom of eSwatini.
